# Cūḷabyūha Sutta (Snp 4.12 (PTS Snp 171))

**ID:** Snp 4.12 (PTS Snp 171)
**Section:** Suttanipāta (snp)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Cūḷabyūha Sutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0505m.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

In modern scholarship on early Buddhism, the sutta has been analyzed in debates regarding early Buddhist epistemological and mystical stances: researchers highlight its dismissal of dogmas, theories, and *saññā* (perception, verse 886), as well as its discussion of sectarians (*titthyā*, verses 891–892) and the figure of the *brāhmaṇa* who accomplishes the religious goal without adhering to canonical doctrines [Seyfort Ruegg and Schmithausen 1990].

 DharmaNexus additionally generates machine-based alignments with the Chinese *Qishi yinben jing* (T 25, 起世因本經), albeit with low similarity scores [DharmaNexus]. In Pali literature, the sutta forms the subject of an entire section of the canonical commentary, the *Cūḷabyūhasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 12) in the *Mahāniddesa*, with which DharmaNexus records extensive text reuse across 82 matching passages (over 7,700 characters, notably at segments §6.4–9.1) [DharmaNexus]. Further shared passages appear in the traditional commentaries, the *Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathā* and the *Mahāniddesa-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].
